page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a handwritten annotation in the right margin (ignored as handwriting, described in notes); running head at top; page number at top right; signature mark at foot right in handwriting (not transcribed). Epigram headings are set in italic, centred.

main_text.l: Hoc vt ego vitem, sed sedulus assequar illud
Si detur: dabitur res pretiosa mihi.

l.i: Ad votum eiusdem, Panca habere, & nul-

main_text.l: Quantas Croesus opes habuit, nec scire laboro,
Nec mihi tam magnas opto petóve dari.
Iri nec triftem mendici poltulo fortem:
Nam res eximias non finit illa geri.
Non egeam satis est: vt abundem negligo: durum
Est vt habere nihil, sic & habere nimis,
Verùm, quicquid ero, semper fors illa placebit,
Quae sancti stabit numinis arbitrio.
Aëra per vacuum volitantes suspice pappos,
Canities demum quos facit ipsa leues.
Constanter fixi iuuenili in caule manebant:
Fluxilis in veteri sed mouet aura scapo.
His nonnullorum mores conferre licebit:
Qui iuuenes sapiunt, desipiúntque senes.
Centaurus datus est morum formator Achilli,
Graiorum veluti prisca camoena refert.
Prudentis, fortisque ducis sic pingitur
εἰκὼν, Nam vir consilio, robore pollet equus.
Esse nequit scabies vsquam scabiosior vlla,
Quàm religans mentes vana superstitio.

page.notes: The handwritten marks in the right margin (a bracket, "§", "ouē", "vnsev", "Εἰς Σαμουίαν", etc.) and the underlining in the text are manuscript annotations, not printed; the Greek word in the Centaurus epigram is a best reading of a handwritten-looking or printed εἰκών. Lines are transcribed as paragraphs; the Latin verse lines are run together within stanzas where the scan's line breaks were uncertain.
